parts.visual:
You acquire 100 users for your new photo-sharing app. Each of those 100 users invites 2 friends. Now you have 300 users. Those 200 new users invite 2 friends each. The app spreads like a virus. You spend exactly $0 on marketing.

The Viral Math:
1. The Viral Coefficient (K-Factor): A mathematical formula that calculates how many new users each existing user brings into the product.
2. The Threshold: If K is less than 1 (e.g., 0.5), the viral loop will eventually stop. If K is greater than 1 (e.g., 1.2), the app will experience exponential, infinite growth until it saturates the entire market.
parts.audio: Virality is not an accident; it is an engineered mathematical function. You do not 'hope' your product goes viral; you build specific mechanisms into the software to force the K-factor above 1.

questions.question: A startup builds an app where users can track their personal diet. The K-factor is 0.1. Why?
options: Lack of Inherent Social Value. Tracking your diet is a solo activity. There is no natural reason to invite your friends to the app, because their presence doesn't make the app better for you. Single-player mode destroys virality.
Because the app is too expensive.
questions.correct_answer: Lack of Inherent Social Value. Tracking your diet is a solo activity. There is no natural reason to invite your friends to the app, because their presence doesn't make the app better for you. Single-player mode destroys virality.
questions.explanation: Multiplayer mode is the foundation of the K-Factor.

questions.question: Listen to the famous growth hack used by Hotmail in 1996. What was the viral mechanism?
questions.tts_text: We didn't have money for ads. So we just added one line of text to the bottom of every single email our users sent: 'P.S. Get your free email at Hotmail.' Every email sent became a billboard.
options: Inherent Virality. The user doesn't even have to 'try' to invite someone. Simply by using the product (sending an email), they are automatically broadcasting the product to a non-user. The product itself is the marketing channel.
They paid users to send emails.
questions.correct_answer: Inherent Virality. The user doesn't even have to 'try' to invite someone. Simply by using the product (sending an email), they are automatically broadcasting the product to a non-user. The product itself is the marketing channel.
questions.explanation: This hack acquired 12 million users in 18 months.

questions.question: What is an 'Incentivized Viral Loop' (like Dropbox used)?
options: Paying the user in digital value to invite friends. Dropbox said: 'If you invite a friend, we will give both you and your friend 500MB of extra storage space for free.' It aligns the user's greed with the company's growth.
Threatening to delete the user's account.
questions.correct_answer: Paying the user in digital value to invite friends. Dropbox said: 'If you invite a friend, we will give both you and your friend 500MB of extra storage space for free.' It aligns the user's greed with the company's growth.
questions.explanation: If the product isn't naturally viral, you must buy the virality with digital perks.

questions.question: Why is 'Viral Cycle Time' just as important as the K-Factor?
options: Because it controls the velocity of the outbreak. If your K-Factor is 2, but it takes a user 6 months to invite 2 friends, your growth is slow. If it takes them 6 seconds (like sharing a TikTok video), your company explodes overnight.
questions.correct_answer: Because it controls the velocity of the outbreak. If your K-Factor is 2, but it takes a user 6 months to invite 2 friends, your growth is slow. If it takes them 6 seconds (like sharing a TikTok video), your company explodes overnight.

pairs.match: The mathematical number of new users generated by one existing user
When the normal usage of the product automatically advertises it to others
Giving users a digital reward (like storage space) for inviting friends
How quickly a new user successfully invites another new user
